before: Automated sentiment analysis may change the direction of comparisons between groups of social-media messages. We audited human labels and archived VADER and Twitter RoBERTa predictions for 14,640 airline tweets and 4,483 unique debate tweets. Outcomes were group negative-share error and strict pairwise ranking reversal. VADER reversed 3/15 airline comparisons; RoBERTa reversed none. Both reversed 7/45 debate comparisons, including three VADER and two RoBERTa reversals among pairs with human-reference gaps of at least ten percentage points. At 400 airline labels per group, group-specific shrunk ACC reduced VADER error, but direct human estimation performed better. RoBERTa group-specific ACC had slightly lower prevalence MAE than human-only estimation (2.61 versus 2.66 percentage points), but more ranking reversals. At 100 debate labels per group, human-only estimation outperformed all tested corrections. Retaining repeated debate texts changed VADER reversals to 16/45; majority-label and cross-group-duplicate sensitivities preserved the primary counts. Shrinkage and comparison-set sensitivities supported evaluating prevalence and ordering separately. These retrospective results describe message-level negativity in selected historical archives; the original RoBERTa inference environment was not recoverable. The practical contribution is an auditable workflow that evaluates the comparisons a sentiment measure supports.

before: The reproducibility boundary is equally specific. Original input hashes and row alignment match, and both budget protocols reproduce the archived summaries, but exact historical model and library versions remain unavailable. This supports statistical reproduction from stored predictions, not restoration of original neural inference. Split and bootstrap repetitions reuse archive records; their percentile ranges are conditional, and pairwise comparisons are dependent. The two archived shrinkage implementations differ slightly and k = 100 is not optimal across all tasks; the new grid is a sensitivity analysis, not out-of-sample model selection. Fixed complete-archive and held-out-only gap definitions target different pair sets. Finally, exact supervised-data matching does not exclude approximate or pretraining exposure, and neither strict inversions nor half-penalty ties quantify the decision cost of an incorrect comparison.
